title: The Redemption Value per Point on a Settlement of Billed Charges, by Savings Relationship
content:
On a card under Personal Credit Cards, the redemption value used to turn a settlement of billed charges into a point count is read from the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

1. Where the cardholder holds an active savings account whose balance is at least 25000.00 USD and at least 1 savings interest credit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months, the redemption value is 0.0125 USD a point.

2. Where the cardholder holds an active savings account whose balance is below 25000.00 USD and at least 1 savings interest credit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months, the redemption value is 0.011 USD a point.

3. Where neither of those holds, the redemption value is the tier's own cash value per point.

**On the two parts.** Each of the first two conditions requires an active savings account of the stated balance and at least 1 savings interest credit in the last three months together. A cardholder with an active savings balance of 40000.00 USD but no savings interest credit in the last three months falls in the third case; so does a cardholder with savings interest credits in that window who holds no active savings account.

**What the difference is worth.** On a hypothetical covered amount of 132.00 USD, a redemption value of 0.0125 USD a point gives a quotient of 10560 points, one of 0.011 USD a point gives 12000 points, and a tier cash value of 0.01 USD a point gives 13200 points: the higher the value per point, the fewer points the same settlement uses. A balance of exactly 25000.00 USD belongs to the first case, the test being at least that amount.
